newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Carter withdraws appeal in Copec dispute.
newsitem.headline: Carter withdraws appeal in Copec dispute.

text.p: New Zealand forestry group Carter Holt Harvey Ltd said on Wednesday it had withdrawn an appeal in the Chilean Supreme Court in a dispute with the Angelini group with which it owns 60 percent of Chilean industrial conglomerate Copec.
"We decided for a number of reasons that we would not continue to ask for that particular one to be heard in the court process," Bruce Waters, operating counsel for CHH, told Reuters.
"But there are a number of legal actions still on foot. The major actions are in play and nothing has changed," he said.

A spokesman for Angelini, Fernando Aguero, said the withdrawal was a "significant procedural victory" and was the latest in a series of setbacks for International Paper - controlled CHH in its attempt to overturn their joint venture.
But Waters said it would be a misreading to suggest the appeal withdrawal was an issue of "underlying significance".
Angelini and CHH have been in legal dispute for three years since CHH attempted to gain direct ownership of its Copec (Compania de Petroleos de Chile SA) stake and get on the board.
So far CHH has failed in its attempt to have the joint venture with Angelini held through Inversiones y Desarrollo Los Andes S.A. (Los Andes) dissolved.
Angelini Group has management control on Copec until 2007 and over two years ago it countersued to have CHH expelled from Los Andes for alleged repeated breaches of their agreement.
Aguero said in a statement CHH withdrew the appeal minutes before the hearing was to take place.

"We are pleased that by abandoning the appeal, even though at the last minute, Carter Holt Harvey has finally accepted Angelini's position that the arbitrator is the correct person to deal with Carter Holt's claims," Aguero said.
However, Waters said CHH still may not accept arbitration.
"We may decide not to take it to the arbitrator at all."
Aguero said arbitrator Juan Colombo had indicated he would rule in 1997 on the Angelini claim to expell CHH from Los Andes.
But Waters said CHH remains confident it will not be expelled from Los Andes.
"We are confident that we will repel it. The longer that action goes, the less concern we have that our position is deteriorating."
